reviewer.notes: Re-ran named probes on this Linux worktree. Probe (b) independently parsed sweep-reservation-enabled-scheduler-events.jsonl and joined every interactive_dispatched row to a batch_deferred row with reason reserved_interactive_headroom. Comment-only and reserved_slots=0 mutants both go red. CLOUD-OK harvest UNIT-COMPLETE is not delivery.

defects.summary: B07 is an allocation bucket (ready_units BUCKET_SATISFIED). A runnable shared-subscription scheduler with numeric reserved slots now lives in assert_reservation.py and was executed live.
Named probes run_named_probes.py and assert_reservation.py exist and re-run to exit 0 with on-disk raws.
Condition 11 is registered on the per-unit UNIT-ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json. Global unit_manifest.py --check sibling red is out of this unit's scope.

downstream_consumers.consumer: probe-b independent jsonl join of interactive arrivals to batch deferrals

retry.policy: Two cloud-ok file-only strikes then pivot: restore the named probe tree and bind a runnable reserved-headroom scheduler rather than hand-flip state=SUCCESS.

residual_unknowns.claim: tools/command-center/measure_rate.py remains a register-gate firing-rate meter and does not implement reserved headroom.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Out of scope for TST-0140; the bound scheduler is assert_reservation.SharedSubscriptionScheduler.

report.measured_answer: Yes: with a saturating four-slot batch sweep, the bound scheduler keeps interactive p95 inside the latency budget by reserving one slot, observable as a refused/deferred batch dispatch at each interactive arrival. Disabling the numeric reservation, or replacing it with a config comment, makes the assertion go red.

extensions.title: Interactive lane keeps reserved headroom against a batch sweep
extensions.question_or_target: With a batch sweep saturating the shared subscription, does an interactive request still get served within its latency budget? PASS requires: a measurable reservation (not a documented intention), and the reservation must be observable as a refused/deferred batch dispatch at the moment the interactive request arrives.
